title: Control flow
description: if, while, for, and match in C#

exercises.title: If Statement
exercises.description: Declare age = 20. If age >= 18, Console.WriteLine Adult. Otherwise Console.WriteLine Minor.
exercises.starter_code:
var age = 20;
// if (age >= 18) Console.WriteLine("Adult"); else Console.WriteLine("Minor");
hints: Compare integers with standard C# relational operators.

exercises.title: For Loop
exercises.description: Use a for loop to Console.WriteLine numbers 1 through 5.
hints: A `for` loop with inclusive bounds uses `var i = 1; i <= 5; i++`.
Emit one integer per iteration with its own newline when required.

exercises.title: Switch Statement
exercises.description: Declare day = 2. Use a switch statement to Console.WriteLine the day name: 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, default=Unknown.
hints: Switch on the `day` primitive with labeled `case` branches and terminating `break;`.

exercises.title: For-Range Loop
exercises.description: Create a slice colors = list["red", "green", "blue"}. Use for ... in to Console.WriteLine each color on its own line.
exercises.starter_code:
var colors = new[] { "red", "green", "blue" };
// foreach (var c in colors) Console.WriteLine(c);
hints: Model the collection as `new[] { ... }` or `List<string>`; iterate with `foreach`.
exercises.solution:
var colors = new[] { "red", "green", "blue" };
foreach (var c in colors) Console.WriteLine(c);

exercises.title: Else If Chain
exercises.description: Declare score = 85. Print the grade: 90+ = A, 80+ = B, 70+ = C, 60+ = D, below 60 = F.
exercises.starter_code:
var score = 85;
// chain if / else if for grade
hints: Chain conditions from highest thresholds downward (≥90 ⇒ A…).
Ternary ladders or cascading `else if` both work.

exercises.title: For Loop with Break
exercises.description: Use a for loop to count from 1 upward. When i reaches 5, break out of the loop. Print each number before the break.
exercises.starter_code:
var i = 1;
// while / for with break at 5
hints: Increment a counter forever (`for (;;)`) until `break` fires at the cutoff.
Print numbers before branching out of the loop when that matches the checker.

exercises.title: Continue Statement
exercises.description: Use a for loop to Console.WriteLine numbers 1 to 10, but skip Console.WriteLineing even numbers using continue.
exercises.starter_code: for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { /* skip evens */ }
hints: Use `%` parity checks and `continue` to skip undesired iterations.
Loop inclusively across the requested numeric range.
